carrs_manager.text: Carr's of Carlisle. Founded in 1831 by Jonathan Dodgson Carr, a Quaker from Kendal who baked a plain, crisp biscuit that kept for months on a ship. That was his genius. It kept.

He later sent them to Queen Victoria, and the firm got a royal warrant. We still make the Table Water biscuit here, in Carlisle, where it is for eating with cheese. People eat them with jam. We tolerate this.
Mind the ovens. They're hot, and the biscuits will be in the tin before you're out the door.

carrs_baker.text: The big secret of a water biscuit is that it has hardly any. Flour, a bit of fat, and water. You roll it so thin you can read the rolling pin through it.
My nan said Carr's was the only reason anyone south of Penrith had heard of Carlisle. She's not entirely wrong.
